claim: Mariana Tek sells boutique fitness software to studios and franchises.
quote: Boutique fitness software that's trusted by single locations, fitness franchises, and anything in-between.

claim: Admin API: its primary API, the control arm for backend and business needs; tools for fitness business administration.
quote: Admin API - Our primary API serves as the control arm for your backend and business needs. Build tools for the fitness business administration using this interface

claim: Customer API: bespoke customer experiences, built from the customer's perspective.
quote: Customer API - Build bespoke customer experiences with an intuitive API built from the customer perspective

claim: Studio API: endpoints to manage studio configurations.
quote: Studio API - Purpose built endpoints to manage your studio configurations

claim: MT Stripe API: a custom checkout flow on Mariana Tek's Stripe integration.
quote: MT Stripe API - Leverage Mariana Tek's Stripe Integration and build a custom checkout flow

claim: Documents API: waivers, documents and contracts.
quote: Documents API - Create and manage unique waivers, documents and contracts to connect with your customers

claim: Pricing API: pricing control.
quote: Pricing API - Fine tune your pricing control and optimize your market strategy

claim: Webhooks: notifications about account events.
quote: Webhooks - Build efficient and responsive software based on account events

claim: Custom development for a studio's website uses the pre-built Web Integrations, the Customer API, or both.
quote: Integrate Mariana Tek functionality into studio websites by using our pre-built Web Integrations , leveraging our Customer API for bespoke customer experiences, or mixing these approaches.

claim: A studio app extends the Admin Application with the Admin API, and can use the Pricing Engine to change class prices dynamically.
quote: Help studio owners manage their business by extending our Admin Application using our Admin API to build a standalone integration. You can also use our Pricing Engine to dynamically change class registration prices.

claim: A customer app used by one or many studios combines the Customer API with Universal Authentication.
quote: Add functionality to customer-facing websites that can be used by one or many studios and integrated seamlessly with our Universal Authentication and the Customer API .

claim: A booking app that partners with many studios uses Bypass Bookings.
quote: Extend your reach by partnering with multiple studios on Mariana Tek to give your users access to some of the top brands in the industry with Bypass Bookings .

claim: The Customer API is described in an OpenAPI document at https://docs.marianatek.com/api/customer/v1/schema/ ... (the document's description says the Customer API uses OpenAPI; the quote ends where a link begins).
quote: The Customer API uses OpenAPI with

claim: ... which Mariana Tek introduces as giving you the power to build custom booking and buying experiences for fitness customers.
quote: Mariana Tek's Customer API gives you the power to build custom booking and buying experiences for fitness customers.

claim: To register an application and get OAuth credentials, the credentials guide says to contact integrations@marianatek.com ...
quote: In order to register your application and get credentials to start authenticating via OAuth, please contact integrations@marianatek.com .

claim: ... and the same address manages API keys.
quote: To manage your applications and credentials, please contact integrations@marianatek.com .

claim: Mariana Tek's FAQ describes a Developer Portal for managing sandbox integrations, generating credentials and starting a technical review, but says it is in Beta and not uniformly available yet.
quote: The Developer Portal is a self-service interface designed for developers and development teams which allows you to manage the integrations in your sandbox, generate credentials, initiate a technical review and prepare your app for the live production environment. It is currently in Beta and is not uniformly available yet.

claim: The sandbox is a mock studio seeded with sample data, with its own tenant name, sandbox API and Web Integrations, almost identical to production.
quote: A sandbox is a mock studio client that developers can leverage to build and test integrations. The sandbox is a demo environment which is almost identical to the live production environment in appearance and features, and is seeded with sample data. This means there is a tenant name (MT subdomain), sandbox API, and Web Integrations platform associated with the sandbox, the same as a live studio.

claim: Every studio, live or sandbox, is addressed by its tenant name (the MT subdomain), and the sandbox API lives at https://{tenant_name}.marianatek.com/api.
quote: The tenant name or MT Subdomain is the name used to identify a specific live studio or sandbox and is required to access the API and set up Web Integrations. The URL needed to access the sandbox API is https://{tenant_name}.marianatek.com/api

claim: Sandbox tenant names often end in .sandbox.
quote: Sandbox tenants most often include the suffix ".sandbox" as part of the tenant name

claim: Integration partners get access to their sandbox Admin App during onboarding.
quote: Integration partners will obtain email and password access to their sandbox Admin App during the onboarding/build process with Mariana Tek.

claim: Mariana Tek accepts two kinds of credential: OAuth 2.0 client credentials and API keys.
quote: There are two types of application credentials that can be used in order to make authenticated requests with Mariana Tek: API keys and OAuth2.0 client credentials.

claim: OAuth when requests should act for an end user: apps that need a studio owner or customer to log in, user-scoped views and profiles, or single sign-on.
quote: OAuth - Applications requiring studio owner or customer login, user scoped views, user profiles, or single sign on capabilities.

claim: Single-page and mobile apps must use OAuth.
quote: If you are building a Single Page Application (SPA) or a mobile application, OAuth2.0 credentials will be required.

claim: An API key, tied to a service account for your application ...
quote: requests which are authenticated with OAuth2.0 will be tied to the end user, whereas those authenticated with an API key will be tied to the service account associated with your application

claim: ... when you manipulate data for many users without any one user's login.
quote: API Key - Applications requiring app level data manipulations for multiple users, without a specific user's input or login needed.

claim: You choose the service user's permissions when you register.
quote: In order to use an API key for authentication, you will need to register your application and select the desired permissions for your service user.

claim: Mariana Tek says never to commit API keys to version control or use them in client-side code.
quote: In particular, you should not commit these keys to version control or use them in client-side code.

claim: Both credentials are sent with bearer authentication (API keys).
quote: To make an authenticated request with an API key, bearer authentication should be used:

claim: Both credentials are sent with bearer authentication (OAuth access tokens).
quote: Mariana Tek's APIs use bearer auth for authenticating requests.

claim: Mariana Tek supports the Authorization Code flow for confidential clients and the Authorization Code flow with PKCE for public clients.
quote: Mariana Tek supports the Authorization Code flow for confidential applications and the Authorization Code w/ PKCE flow for public applications.

claim: Confidential clients are server-side web apps; public clients are single-page and mobile apps.
quote: For example, single-page applications and mobile applications are considered public, whereas server-side web applications are typically confidential.

claim: Both run on the brand's own subdomain (the subdomain parameter).
quote: The subdomain corresponding to the brand where the user is attempting to log in.

claim: PKCE adds code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256.
quote: We recommend that this is always set to S256 , which indicates that the code_challenge is the SHA256 hash of the code_verifier .

claim: state is required, and Mariana Tek tells you to check it on the callback to prevent CSRF.
quote: To prevent CSRF attacks, you should verify that the value of state matches the one you set as part of Step 1.

claim: prompt=True forces a login even when the user already has a session. Without it, a user with an active session is sent straight back to your redirect_uri.
quote: If the user already has an active session and you have not set the prompt query parameter to True , then the user will not prompted to log in again and will be immediately redirected back to the redirect_uri

claim: The token request includes the redirect_uri (required; defaults when only one is configured).
quote: The URL provided as part of step 1. If your app only has one redirect_uri configured, that value is used as a default.

claim: The example token response has expires_in of 604800 seconds, which is seven days, along with a refresh_token.
quote: "expires_in" : 604800

claim: Exchange the refresh token with grant_type=refresh_token ...
quote: For refresh tokens, the value should always be set to refresh_token .

claim: ... confidential clients also send their client_secret.
quote: Note: Confidential type clients must also append the client_secret in the above refresh_token request string.

claim: The redirect URL must match the registered one exactly; usual causes of a mismatch error: no redirect URL registered yet, a typo, a trailing backslash on only one of the two URLs, URL encoding, or an old URL still registered.
quote: These strings must match exactly; the most common issues encountered that cause these errors are: You have not provided a redirect URL for your OAuth flow yet, there is a typo in the redirect URL, there's a trailing backslash on only one URL string, there's an error related to URL encoding, or you have updated your redirect URL and the former one is still registered for your application.

claim: Mariana Tek can post events to your URL, for example when a customer creates an account, makes a reservation or checks in to class.
quote: For example, you can rely on webhooks to trigger an action in your app/integration when a customer creates an account, makes a reservation, or checks in to class.

claim: There is no self-serve subscription in the guides: you ask Integrations.
quote: Please contact integrations@marianatek.com to start using webhooks.

claim: You give your HTTPS subscriber URL ...
quote: Your subscriber URL ( Note: This must use https protocol)

claim: ... the events you want ...
quote: The webhook event posts you would like to subscribe to

claim: ... and the environment.
quote: The environment you are working in (i.e. the sandbox or production URL)

claim: For a studio's production environment, Integrations needs the studio owner's approval by email.
quote: To set up webhooks for a studio's production environment, you must have approval from the Studio Owner sent to Integrations by email.

claim: A one-click-install integration can be switched on for a new studio from one bundle of credentials ...
quote: A one-click-install is an integration that uses a bundle of credentials which allows us to easily enable it on new studio clients, and ensures compatibility with our future roadmap.

claim: ... and for webhooks that requires subscriber URLs that are identical across clients or differ only by the MT subdomain.
quote: The subscriber URLs that you generate to accept MT webhook posts must either be identical across clients or differ ONLY by the MT Subdomain .

claim: Before going live with a studio, you may have to pass a technical review ...
quote: Before you go live with a Mariana Tek Studio Client, you may need to submit your integration for technical review and approval.

claim: ... Mariana Tek says not every app needs one.
quote: Not all apps are required for technical review

claim: The integration must be fully built and tested in the sandbox first.
quote: Your integration should be completely built and fully tested in the sandbox environment before submitting for technical review.

claim: The submission covers how the integration works ...
quote: Include a detailed description of how the integration works, the features, the user and/or data flow and any necessary additional info

claim: ... the endpoints and webhooks it uses ...
quote: Include a list of API endpoints and webhooks on Mariana Tek's platform that you will be accessing

claim: ... credentialed access to a test environment ...
quote: Provide us credentialed access to an environment where your integration can be viewed and all use cases can be demonstrated.

claim: ... a screen recording ...
quote: Provide a screen recording for a quick overview or walkthrough of how to use the app.

claim: ... and the studios you work with or plan to.
quote: Include a list of studios or Mariana Tek clients you are working with or intend to work with

claim: Mariana Tek says reviews can take up to 1-3 weeks to complete.
quote: Reviews can take up to 1-3 weeks to complete.

claim: Your account permissions are limited to the endpoints and use cases that were reviewed and approved, and using other endpoints you can reach is not permitted.
quote: Your account permissions will be scoped to the endpoints and use cases that were reviewed and approved. In the event that you have access to endpoints that were not approved for your use, please note that leveraging those endpoints is not permitted.

claim: If a launched integration falls outside the approved guidelines, Mariana Tek discontinues its API access until you work through a consultation with your integration manager.
quote: In the event your integration is launched, but then falls outside of our approved guidelines, we will discontinue your API access.

claim: Mariana Tek lists partners in a marketplace at partners.marianatek.com, including ClassPass ...
quote: ClassPass Flexible fitness & wellness access across studios worldwide

claim: ... Wellhub ...
quote: Wellhub Get new, high-quality members with our corporate clients

claim: ... and Spivi.
quote: Spivi Performance metrics, leaderboards, and loyalty for fitness studios
